title: Hootie Green and the Frog Pond in Newbern
summary: As a boy he sat in on drums with the Frog Pond's resident pianist Hootie Green, and recalls the lack of bars.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: When you were a boy, before running away from home, do you recall seeing or hearing any musicians come through town, traveling musicians who may have played Ragtime or other kinds of, say, Cakewalk music?

The only musicians who come through town there was playing... They were playing the same kind of music we was playing. But I just made up my mind I wanted to leave home, run away from home at that age... Around nine, ten, eleven years old, twelve, I had some nights I'd go up to the Frog Pond and sit in on the drums. And they had a little band there. They had some good musicians there in Newbern, North Carolina. But you couldn't get them out of there.
They had some very good musicians there. The piano player was Hootie Green. He was one of the greatest piano players around.
And he played a lot of the popular songs of the day?

Yeah. Whatever he played, he had a very good left hand. Something like Fats Waller. He didn't do no singing; he just played. But he always liked good drumming. He had his own drums with him. The drums would be out there. So he told me... He'd been there about ten years, in one place. That's all he used at the Frog Pond.
So the Frog Pond was a dance hall.
Was there any playing of music in taverns or bars or any restaurants in any of the nearby cities and towns?

Well, I don't know too much about barroom... I don't think too many bars was open during that time. I remember, I used to go out on the street and pick up bottles... I guess there must have been barrooms open for it to have them whiskey bottles. I'd go pick up the whiskey bottles, Coca-Cola bottles, and sell them. I used to get two or three cents a bottle for them bottles. Now they call them taverns...I don't know what they call them... They call them bars. I don't think they had the bars during that time... But anyway, I was so young, I wasn't allowed in them
I see. So Hootie Green was the big... He was the most well-known musician in that area, I take it.
I see. And he had a drummer. Do you recall seeing or hearing other musicians sit in with him at the dance hall? A trumpet player maybe, or a cornet player or clarinet player?
No. I don't remember any of the others. I just remember this particular one.
